title: The Blaschka Object Network — Dealer Sales Print Register
scope: Dealer-produced or dealer-distributed catalogues, pamphlets, bulletins and exhibition sales print used to reconstruct how natural-history objects and Blaschka models were converted into selectable, priced and orderable commodities.
evidence_guard: A dealer catalogue is direct Blaschka evidence only when the source or a precise archival description identifies Blaschka models. General dealer catalogues are commercial controls. A catalogue known through a published archival citation is kept distinct from a currently verified digital item record.

records.dealer: Václav Frič / V. Frič natural-history business
records.extent: 43-page catalogue reported in published archival research
records.evidence: J. P. Short cites a forty-three-page Frič naturalia catalogue at this archival locator and reports that it offered Blaschka holothurians, corals, medusae and sea anemones among a much wider range of naturalia. The catalogue marketed glass imitations of sea creatures as a way to teach inland schools about organisms difficult to preserve or observe.
records.research_value: A direct dealer-side witness to category placement: Blaschka models were sold inside a broad natural-history catalogue rather than through an isolated art-glass market. This permits page-level comparison of models with reptiles, fishes, crustaceans, insects, birds, mammals and other commodities in the same sales environment.
records.catalogue_guard: The exact 29/139 item has not yet been cross-walked to a modern item-level CalmView record in this pass. The archival locator is retained as a precise published citation and should be verified against the physical or scanned file before quoting catalogue wording from the original.

records.repository: Academy of Natural Sciences of Drexel University Archives
records.evidence: The related Blaschka archival description identifies the Ward pamphlet as advertising Blaschka glass models and Ward's American agency, with customers directed toward the glass-model catalogue.
records.research_value: Direct evidence that agency status and catalogue access were publicly marketed to North-American customers.

records.repository: Biodiversity Heritage Library / Smithsonian Libraries and Archives
records.evidence: Public-domain run of the firm's own bulletin, available for issue- and page-level searching.
records.research_value: Can recover the firm's commercial rhetoric, product categories, customers and announcements during the mature Blaschka-distribution period.
records.blaschka_guard: No page is promoted as Blaschka-specific until inspected and verified.

records.author: Samuel Pickworth Woodward
records.title: Generic catalogue of recent & fossil shells
records.evidence: A complete public-domain copy survives through the Biodiversity Heritage Library / Internet Archive. The imprint explicitly states that it was printed for R. Damon in Weymouth.
records.research_value: Shows Damon using printed systematic cataloguing as commercial infrastructure two decades before the Blaschka agency. It is a baseline for later model catalogues and dealer/customer list practices.
records.blaschka_guard: Predates the Blaschka agency and concerns recent and fossil shells.

records.title: A catalogue of the shells of Great Britain and Ireland with their synonyms and authorities
records.evidence: Biodiversity Heritage Library catalogues the volume under Robert Damon with Weymouth imprint R. Damon.
records.research_value: An earlier Damon catalogue establishing his use of taxonomy, synonymy and printed lists as part of a dealer/collector knowledge economy.

records.title: Exposition universelle de 1889, à Paris: V. Frič, Naturaliste à Prague, 1544-II (Bohême Autriche)
records.extent: pp. 1–4, as cited in museum research
records.evidence: Grant Museum research cites the four-page Paris exhibition guide while discussing Frič's marketed preparations and teaching material.
records.research_value: Places catalogue-style sales presentation inside an international exhibition environment at the end of the marine-model period.
records.source_guard: A standalone digitised primary copy has not been isolated in this pass; retain as a bibliographic retrieval target rather than a transcribed source.

research_observation: Sales print was an operating technology of the dealer network. Catalogues and bulletins classified objects into selectable units, supplied names and numbers, framed educational uses and gave customers a vocabulary for ordering at distance. The Frič catalogue is especially important because it places Blaschka models inside the same commercial taxonomy as natural specimens and other teaching material.
